title: Replicating Induction Head Circuit in a Byte-Level Language Model: Does Tokenization Affect Head Formation?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Tests whether mechanistic interpretability findings are tokenization-dependent. If induction heads are artifacts of BPE tokenization, many published findings may not generalize. This is methodologically important but the link to a concrete safety action is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training a small byte-level transformer from scratch using nanoGPT-style code is feasible on medium compute. However, adapting the prefix matching score to byte sequences and comparing to published results requires custom implementation. Beginners need strong guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two phases: training the byte-level model and analyzing induction head formation. Training is straightforward but the analysis requires adapting existing metrics. Comparison to published BPE results adds interpretation work. Feasible but stretches 30 hours.
